observations.claim: Metformin product identity includes its release formulation, tablet strength and intended dosing schedule. The immediate-release and extended-release labels describe different administration patterns; an extended-release tablet is designed to release its contents over time and is swallowed whole, rather than crushed or chewed. An immediate-release regimen used in a trial therefore cannot be converted into an extended-release research regimen simply by matching the total milligrams. The two products also have their own dose-increase instructions and labeled limits. FDA-approved generic products must meet the relevant requirements for the reference product, including active ingredient, strength, dosage form, route and bioequivalence. That regulatory comparison concerns a specified reference formulation. It does not establish that every release formulation, compounded preparation or differently scheduled product reproduces the exposure or clinical findings of a particular repurposing trial.
